To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the optical properties of 2- quinolinone-based compounds can be tuned by introducing electron-withdrawn substituents and by alkylation.
the optical properties of 2- quinolinone can be tuned by the presence of acceptor groups, and alkylation at the N-position retains charge-transfer transition.
N- vs. 2-alkylated 2-quinolones show different photophysical and thermal properties and these properties can be tuned by changing the alkylation site and the acceptor groups.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the synthesis of 2- quinolinone derivatives, which are potential building blocks for the construction of organic semiconductors and optoelectronic materials, and the investigation of the photophysical properties of these derivatives.
the synthesis of new 2-quinolone derivatives with three different acceptors, which are N- and O-alkyl derivatives.
the synthesis and characterisation of 2- quinolinone-based donor–acceptor compounds with three different acceptors (CN, CF3 and C6F5) and their N- and O-alkyl derivatives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of a quinolinone ring in these compounds plays a vital role in tuning their properties.
the N-alkyl group has a greater impact on the electronic properties of the quinolinones compared with the O-alkyl group, which has been supported by the experimental and theoretical studies.
the N- and O-alkylations in the quinoline moiety have a profound effect on the optical properties of the compounds, which can be tuned by the introduction of electron-withdrawing groups.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a series of 2-quionolinone-based compounds that have tunable optical properties through simple alkylation.
we were able to tune the optical and thermal properties of 2-alkylated 2-quinolone compounds by introducing electron-with-drawing acceptors.
the N-alkyl quinolinone compound has a large Stokes shift and a high quantum yield, which makes it a good candidate for fluorescent probes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optical properties of 2- quinolinone-based molecules can be tuned through simple alkylation.
the optical properties of quinolinone-based molecules can be tuned by N- vs. 0-alkylation.
the N/O-alkylation can be used as a tool to modulate the optical properties of the quinolinones.
